max: Quick question — trying to run an nsys capture inside a k8s pod and the tracefile can't be created: permission denied. Pod has GPUs attached but not privileged.

dena: Are you using the nvidia-container-toolkit runtime in the pod spec? We usually need device mounts for /dev/nvidia* plus access to /proc and /sys for nvml. Also some distros block ptrace without CAP_SYS_PTRACE.

mike: If you're getting EACCES on the output file, it might be the container's tmp dir ownership. What command are you running?

max: Running this from inside the container: `nsys profile -o /tmp/model-trace --trace=cuda,cudnn --duration=10s ./serving_binary`

max: Error log:
```
nsys: ERROR: Unable to write file '/tmp/model-trace.qdrep': Permission denied (EACCES)
```

sara: Two common fixes we've used: 1) mount an explicit emptyDir with fsGroup to the pod so non-root processes can write, or 2) run the capture from an init container with elevated caps and copy the file out.

mike: We had a subtle one last week — `nvidia-container-runtime` will expose devices but not grant capabilities needed for kernel tracing. For full kernel timelines you need either privileged or `securityContext.capabilities.add: ["SYS_ADMIN","SYS_PTRACE"]` (double-check org policy).

dena: Also watch out for the node kernel module permissions: on some nodes `/sys/kernel/tracing` is mode 600 for root only. nsys may try to read perf events and fall back to coarser timers, which hides kernel-selection hotspots.

max: Thanks. I switched to privileged on a test node and could write the qdrep, but the profile shows weird kernel selection: at sequence lengths >1024 we see a sudden jump where GEMM switches to a fallback kernel and latency doubles. Any ideas?

mike: Paste the timeline snippet — curious whether the fused attention kernel is absent or just falling back.

max: Timeline excerpt from nsight (cropped):
```
time(ms)   kernel
0-4        embedding_lookup
4-8        fused_attention_v1 (fast)
8-18       gemm_generic (fallback)  <-- big gap
18-22      fused_attention_v1
```

max: Batching config: dynamic batch up to 8, batch window 5ms. KV cache enabled with file-backed mmap for cold starts.

dena: That fallback often occurs when the runtime picks a kernel based on average sequence length distribution. If a single request spikes seq_len, kernel selection may recompile or choose a different codepath. Check kernel selection logs at `/var/log/redwood/runtime/kernel-choice.log` (we log heuristics there).

mike: Also check whether KV cache mmap file has restrictive permissions — on cold start mmap page faults caused by copy-on-write/deferred reads can delay kernel readiness. If pages are not resident, the first kernels hit page faults and the scheduler can pick a safer generic GEMM to avoid memory pressure.

max: Found this in kernel-choice.log: `seq_len_histogram: median=256 p95=1200 -> selected_kernel=fallback-gemm`. So the heuristics are aggressively conservative when p95 > 1024.

dena: That's expected but we can tweak the heuristic: lower the p95 threshold or prefer the optimized kernel if resident pages > 80%. Suggest adding a residency check after mmap to bias kernel selection.

sara: Ops note — for running profiling at scale in cluster: 1) use a nodepool with `privileged: true` images only for perf jobs, 2) have a cleanup job to chown/chmod trace directories, 3) don't enable on prod nodes.

max: I tried forced re-warm of KV cache (pre-populate mmap) and the gemm stayed the fast variant. So paging was the trigger. Good catch.

mike: Filed an infra ticket to add a CI perf job that runs nsys inside a privileged pod on a ci-node to catch this regression early (ops-bot will create).

ops-bot: created issue RW-4382: "ci/perf: privileged nsys pod job to validate kernel selection under KV-residency" assigned to @mike

max: One follow-up — permissions for the tracefile when userns remap is enabled. We saw qdrep owned by root:root and CI can't collect it. Best pattern?

dena: Recommend mounting an `emptyDir.medium: Memory` backed dir and use `fsGroup` + `runAsUser: 1000` on the pod, then `nsys -o /var/run-traces/model-trace` will be owned correctly. For root-owned trace producers (privileged capture), copy and `chown` in a sidecar.

sara: TL;DR actionable items:
- Add mmap residency check to kernel selection heuristic (eng-runtime)
- Create CI perf job running nsys in privileged pod (eng-infra)
- Add doc snippet for tracefile permissions + recommended pod spec (devex)

max: Thanks everyone — I'll prototype the residency check tomorrow and attach a sample trace to the ticket.

mike: Nice. If you need a reproducible YAML for the privileged pod I can paste ours.

max: Please do, that'd help.
